summary.headline: RSWM Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.7% QoQ to ₹1,161 crore and EBITDA to ₹94 crore (8.0% margin), led by a 39.8% gross margin.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was ₹1,161 crore, up 1.7% QoQ, with domestic sales up to ₹825 crore and exports down to ₹336 crore. Gross margin expanded to 39.8% from 37.4%, lifting EBITDA to ₹94 crore (+10.1% QoQ, +16.1% YoY) and margin to 8.0%. PAT was ₹17 crore against ₹7 crore a year ago, but lower than Q4 FY26, which included a one-time tax benefit. Management gave no full-year guidance; fabric profitability weakened sharply while yarn held up, and new projects (PET food-grade chips, denim garmenting JV, knitting expansion) were outlined.

segments.name: Yarn (synthetic, cotton, mélange)
segments.commentary: Utilisation was about 96% for synthetic, 98% for cotton and 92-93% for mélange. Management said yarn demand held up and cotton/mélange spreads were good in Q1; Q2 is running similarly so far.

segments.name: Denim fabric
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was about 90%. Management said the segment faced the same cost and demand pressure as knit, with exports and domestic roughly balanced.

segments.name: Knit fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation was in the mid-80s%. Fabric EBIT was close to nil in Q1 and was negative (about ₹2 crore) in Q4 FY26, versus about ₹35-36 crore last year, as export garmenters' demand was subdued.

guidance_outlook: No full-year growth or EBITDA margin guidance given; management said all quarters should be similar to or better than Q1.

Power cost savings of about ₹40 crore for FY27 at constant utilisation (from renewables and efficiency), with a stated target of around ₹100 crore; renewable share of power rose from mid-20s% to mid-40s%, and about 60% in the current quarter.
Management expects per-unit power cost to fall by more than ₹1 year-on-year on average.
Knitting expansion expected to add benefits from Q3 FY27, with capacity going from 650 tons to about 900 tons per month, including 150 tons of printing.

Food-grade PET chip plant: completion in Q4 FY27, trials and commercial production in Q1 FY28; 50,000 tpa capacity, ₹500 crore revenue expected, about 15% EBITDA (industry norm per management). Utilisation ramp of 75%, 85%, then 90-91% over three years.
Graphene-based fibre (with Birla Cellulose): management expects commercial traction within FY27.
risks_watch: Crude and polyester price volatility, and a possible reversal of Q1 stocking gains.
Export demand recovery, especially knit fabric and Middle East markets; the company said recent inquiries are improving.
Fabric margins near nil; monitor whether fabric EBIT recovers in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
PET plant execution: food-grade certification and trials, no customer tie-ups yet, and a 15% EBITDA assumption that is management's industry norm.
Garmenting JV: stake and capex undisclosed, new skills needed, and a labour-intensive business that is new to RSWM.
Finance costs rising with working capital needs (₹31 crore).
Management gave no full-year guidance; the company's disclosure is limited on volumes and capex amounts.
Investor-presentation timing: it was uploaded about 15 minutes before the call, which an analyst objected to.
